newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ASTRA, DOLLAR LIFT SWEDISH SHARES HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: ASTRA, DOLLAR LIFT SWEDISH SHARES HIGHER.

text.p: Swedish shares were higher around midday on Monday, lifted by strong gains for drugs major Astra and a recovering dollar.
"The longterm trend is upwards and when we get such temporary setbacks (as this morning) they are seen as a buying opportunity," a trader said.
Traders expected the market to keep trading higher until Wall Street opened and set the direction.
The bourse's general index rose 0.59 percent to 3,247.37 in turnover of 1.90 billion crowns.
Astra rose three to 145 crowns in a rebound.
The upturn was in line with its U.S. close but the share plummeted 10.5 crowns in Stockholm on Friday after posting a lower than six-month expected pre-tax profit for the first six months.
Astra said on Monday its German rival Altana's decision to suspend the clinical development of a successor to its anti-ulcer agent Pantoprazol should strengthen Astra's position longterm.
Investment and medical technology group Incentive jumped 20 crowns to 720 after releasing six-month earnings largely in line with expectations.
The bank sector rose 1.96 percent on continued speculation about a merger of S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken.
S-E-Banken rose 2.5 crowns to 97, Handelsbanken gained 6.5 to 276, Nordbanken jumped seven to 283 and Swedbank was flat at 187.
Telecoms group Ericsson edged one crown higher to 365.
